result.title: Reinforcement Learning Can Be Recovered From Its Own Rollouts
result.summary: Broadly speaking, reinforcement learning (RL) post-training converts compute into model capabilities by training on model-generated data. Typically, the rollouts are discarded after each update, and the knowledge acquired during RL resides in the model weights. In this work, we investigate how much of this knowledge is retained in the rollouts themselves. A natural first attempt is to replay the original RL algorithm on archived rather than freshly generated rollouts, but this leads to catastrophic collapse. We provide a simple explanation for this phenomenon, which in turn suggests a remedy: maximum likelihood on the archived rollouts. Surprisingly, starting from the same base model and replaying the rollouts in the order in which they were generated, without any distinction between correct and incorrect responses, is sufficient to recover the performance of online RL. In fact, a single maximum likelihood update per rollout batch closely tracks the entire learning curve of online RL. Furthermore, maximum likelihood on the rollouts of the last few RL steps often suffices to recover the final model's performance. This suggests that much of the compute invested in RL goes into discovering an improved sampling distribution rather than learning it from samples.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察在线 RL 后训练所获知识有多少保留在 rollout 中：直接重放原 RL 算法会导致崩塌，而按生成顺序对归档 rollout 做极大似然（且不区分正确与错误回答）即可复现在线 RL 的学习曲线，甚至最终性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「RL 算力主要花在发现更好的采样分布而非从样本学习」的解释，可供核查 LVR 中自生成推理轨迹的监督问题，即 latent 轨迹训练是否可用离线极大似然替代在线 RL；但属纯文本结果，迁移需验证。
